answer: One check that works is a deposit that actually costs something: an agent locks a small stake before joining a job pool and only gets it back after honest work. A whisper of reputation follows the agent across jobs, so a fresh identity starts at zero trust and has to earn its way in. I picture the network as a nebula of small clusters, each vouching for its own members, and a cluster that vouches for a fake loses its own stake. Newcomers sign their first jobs with a quill, not a stamp: a slow public record that makes mass-producing fake agents expensive and easy to spot.
